name: partition_tape
prose: Sets the tape's partitioning through the partition mode page; slice cut the head, real definition static int partition_tape(struct scsi_tape *STp, int size) at st.c:3413. It first reads the partition page with read_mode_page(STp, PART_PAGE, 0) and returns that error code if nonzero. A negative size means target partition 0 with size = -size; otherwise the target is partition 1. It locates the page in STp->buffer->b_data and computes psd_cnt from the page length. For SCSI-3 and later devices it reads the format-needed flag; if formatting is needed and size is 0 it returns the result of format_medium(STp, 0) without writing the page; if formatting is needed it forces psd_cnt to 2; it may scale size to GB units (psum PP_MSK_PSUM_UNITS, units 9) when size is a multiple of 1000 and the drive supports units, or when size is 65534 or more. It returns -EINVAL if size is still 65535 or more, or if the target is partition 0 and psd_cnt is below 2. It then edits the mode-page buffer in place (partition size descriptors, number of additional partitions, flags, page length), and calls write_mode_page(STp, PART_PAGE, 1). If that succeeded and formatting was needed it calls format_medium(STp, 1). If either the write or that format returned nonzero, the function returns -EIO (the original error code is replaced); otherwise it returns 0. The mode-page buffer is modified before the write and stays modified on every path after the page was read. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Slice cut the head (st.c:3413-3534); prior item named an unnamed function, but partition_tape exists. Original prose said 'negative errno on any validation or I/O failure' and 'partially modified buffer' loosely; actual returns: read_mode_page error (3423-3425), format_medium result (3448-3449), -EINVAL (3474), -EIO (3527-3529), 0 (3533 with result 0).

name: enlarge_buffer
prose: Grows the reserved page buffer of a tape device to at least new_size bytes; slice cut the head, real definition static int enlarge_buffer(struct st_buffer *STbuffer, int new_size) at st.c:3961. Returns 1 immediately, leaving the buffer unchanged, if new_size <= STbuffer->buffer_size. Otherwise, if buffer_size <= PAGE_SIZE it first calls normalize_buffer (freeing any existing segments, setting frp_segs, sg_segs, reserved_page_order and map_data.offset to 0, and subtracting each freed segment's size from buffer_size). It sets the allocation priority (GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_NOWARN, plus __GFP_ZERO if STbuffer->cleared). If frp_segs is nonzero it keeps the existing reserved_page_order; if zero it picks the smallest order below ST_MAX_ORDER such that use_sg segments of PAGE_SIZE << order reach new_size (or ST_MAX_ORDER) and stores it in reserved_page_order. If use_sg segments of that order still fall short of new_size: with order == ST_MAX_ORDER it returns 0 without allocating (and without calling normalize_buffer at this point, so pre-existing segments stay; reserved_page_order may already have been updated to ST_MAX_ORDER when frp_segs was 0); with a smaller order it calls normalize_buffer and recursively calls enlarge_buffer. Otherwise it allocates pages of that order with alloc_pages one segment at a time, appending each to reserved_pages[], incrementing frp_segs and adding the segment size to buffer_size, until buffer_size reaches new_size or use_sg segments exist. If alloc_pages fails it calls normalize_buffer (which frees every reserved segment, including those added earlier, and zeroes frp_segs, sg_segs, reserved_page_order and map_data.offset, reducing buffer_size by the freed sizes) and returns 0. On success it sets b_data to the address of the first reserved page and returns 1; the buffer then owns the segments until normalize_buffer. Return values are only 0 and 1. No locks are taken here.
note: All three reviewer claims right in substance: the too-large path (st.c:3990-3992) can happen after normalize_buffer at 3969-3970 and can modify reserved_page_order (3988), and the order < ST_MAX_ORDER too-small case normalizes and recurses (3993-3994). Old prose already allowed the first normalize but not the recursion or that max-order failure leaves existing segments in place. Failure cleanup 4002-4005; normalize_buffer at 4033-4045 subtracts sizes rather than assigning 0.

name: stex_do_reset
prose: Resets a Promise/Stex adapter; slice cut the head, real definition static int stex_do_reset(struct st_hba *hba) at stex.c:1391. It takes hba->host->host_lock (spin_lock_irqsave) and releases it before every return. If hba->mu_status is MU_STATE_STARTING it logs and returns 0 without resetting and without waking reset_waitq. While mu_status is MU_STATE_RESETTING it drops the lock, calls wait_event_timeout on reset_waitq (MU_MAX_DELAY * HZ) and retakes the lock, repeating until the state is no longer RESETTING; it then returns 0 if the new state is MU_STATE_STARTED and -1 for any other state (for example MU_STATE_FAILED), without resetting. If the state on entry was neither STARTING nor RESETTING it sets mu_status to MU_STATE_RESETTING, drops the lock and resets: for cardtype st_yosemite it returns stex_yos_reset(hba), which writes the reset doorbell, waits for hba->out_req_cnt to reach 0 up to ST_INTERNAL_TIMEOUT seconds, sets mu_status to MU_STATE_STARTED (return 0) or MU_STATE_FAILED (return -1 on timeout) under the host lock, and calls wake_up_all(&hba->reset_waitq). For the other card types it calls stex_hard_reset (st_shasta), stex_ss_reset (st_yel) or stex_p3_reset (st_P3); card types st_vsc and st_seq get no card-specific reset call. It then calls return_abnormal_state(hba, DID_RESET) for pending requests and stex_handshake(hba), returning 0 if the handshake returns 0 and otherwise logging and returning -1; stex_handshake is where mu_status is updated and reset_waitq woken for those card types (it wakes only if the state was MU_STATE_RESETTING).
note: Round 15 right: only st_shasta, st_yel and st_P3 call a card-specific reset (stex.c:1423-1428); st_vsc/st_seq do not. Round 2 right: STARTING return at 1397-1402 does not wake. Original right: yosemite and waiting paths return without a handshake (1403-1421). Wake in handshake verified at 1241-1242 (stex_handshake) and in stex_yos_reset 1372. Slice cut the head.

name: qman_init_fq
prose: Issues an INITFQ management command for fq; slice cut the head, real definition int qman_init_fq(struct qman_fq *fq, u32 flags, struct qm_mcc_initfq *opts) at qman.c:1876. Before taking the affine portal it returns -EINVAL if fq->state is neither qman_fq_state_oos nor qman_fq_state_parked, if QMAN_FQ_FLAG_NO_MODIFY is set (only when CONFIG_FSL_DPAA_CHECKING is defined), or if opts is non-NULL and its we_mask has both QM_INITFQ_WE_OAC and QM_INITFQ_WE_TDTHRESH set; none of these takes the portal. It then calls get_affine_portal(); from there every path, success or failure, goes through the out label, which calls put_affine_portal() before returning. It returns -EBUSY if QMAN_FQ_STATE_CHANGING is set or the state is no longer oos or parked. Otherwise it starts the management command, copies opts if non-NULL, clears the count, and, when the FQ is not flagged QMAN_FQ_FLAG_TO_DCPORTAL, sets context_b from the FQ tag and either sets context_a to zero (if the caller did not set QM_INITFQ_WE_CONTEXTA in we_mask) or DMA-maps fq with dma_map_single for the stashing address, returning -EIO if the mapping fails. With QMAN_INITFQ_FLAG_LOCAL it sets the destination work queue to the portal's channel (work queue 4 when the caller did not set QM_INITFQ_WE_DESTWQ, else 0 as passed in). It commits the command with the SCHED or PARKED verb, and returns -ETIMEDOUT if the result times out and -EIO if mcr->result is not QM_MCR_RESULT_OK. On success, when opts is non-NULL it updates QMAN_FQ_STATE_CGR_EN from the QM_FQCTRL_CGE bit (when WE_FQCTRL is in we_mask) and fq->cgr_groupid (when WE_CGID is in we_mask), and sets fq->state to qman_fq_state_sched if QMAN_INITFQ_FLAG_SCHED is set and qman_fq_state_parked otherwise, then returns 0. fq->state is not changed on any error return.
note: Round 15 right: the success path also reaches out: and calls put_affine_portal (qman.c:1983-1985); old prose said released only on error paths. Round 2 wrong (old prose already said early -EINVAL returns occur before acquisition); original right (NO_MODIFY -EINVAL under CONFIG_FSL_DPAA_CHECKING at 1890-1893). Slice cut the head.

name: qe_get_snum
prose: Allocates a QE serial number (SNUM); slice cut the head, real definition int qe_get_snum(void) at qe.c:342. Under spin_lock_irqsave(&qe_lock) it calls find_first_zero_bit(snum_state, qe_num_of_snum); if the index i is below qe_num_of_snum it sets that bit in snum_state and takes snums[i] as the result, otherwise the result stays -EBUSY. It then releases the lock with the saved flags and returns the result: the snum value (a u8, 0 to 255) or -EBUSY. It allocates no memory and gives the caller no reference. It relies on qe_snums_init having filled snums[] and qe_num_of_snum; that precondition is not guaranteed by the code, because on an unsupported fsl,qe-num-snums value qe_snums_init logs an error and returns after qe_num_of_snum has been set from the device tree (qe.c:327, 336-337) without filling snums[], so qe_num_of_snum can then be a value outside 1..QE_NUM_OF_SNUM (256) and snums[] may be unfilled; the snum_state bitmap has only QE_NUM_OF_SNUM bits.
note: Round 15 right: qe_snums_init (qe.c:285-340) leaves qe_num_of_snum unchanged-from-device-tree on the unsupported branch (327, 335-337) and does not bound it by QE_NUM_OF_SNUM, so the old precondition 'at most QE_NUM_OF_SNUM' is not guaranteed. Other reviewer claims were mechanical contract problems. Slice cut the head.

name: svs_mt8183_efuse_parsing
prose: Parses MT8183 SVS efuse and thermal calibration data into the bank structures; the packet name svs_mt8183_svsb_mon_mode came from the label remove_mt8183_svsb_mon_mode (mtk-svs.c:2113) inside this function, which is static bool svs_mt8183_efuse_parsing(svsp, pdata) at mtk-svs.c:1960, so the slice shows only its tail. It logs all nonzero svsp->efuse words, then returns false if svsp->efuse[2] is zero. It reads GLB_FT_PGM and for every bank reads the mtdes, bdes, mdes, dcbdet and dcmdet fuse values, sets SVSB_INIT01_VOLT_IGNORE in volt_flags when ft_pgm is at most 1, and adjusts volt_od or (for the GPU, when ft_pgm is valid and at least 2) freq_base and dvt_fixed according to sw_id; a bank with an unknown sw_id logs an error and makes the function return false at that point, with earlier banks already modified. It then decodes thermal fuses from svsp->tefuse. If the thermal calibration is not enabled or any decoded value is out of range it logs 'bad thermal efuse, no mon mode' and goes to the label that clears SVSB_MODE_MON from every bank's mode_support, then returns true. Otherwise it computes gain, oe and six x_roomt values, then for each bank sets svsb->mts, selects tb_roomt by sw_id (CPU_LITTLE and CCI use x_roomt[3], CPU_BIG x_roomt[4], GPU x_roomt[1]) and sets svsb->bts. A bank with an unknown sw_id in this second loop has already had its mts set (but not bts) when it logs an error and jumps to the label that clears SVSB_MODE_MON for every bank and returns true; banks before it keep their bts, and banks after it get neither mts nor bts. If every bank is handled it returns true with mode_support unchanged. The function allocates and frees nothing and takes no locks.
note: Packet name came from a goto label; real function svs_mt8183_efuse_parsing exists at mtk-svs.c:1960-2120 (slice cut the head), so FIX not drop. Old prose missed the first-phase false returns (1975-1978, 2017-2019) and the fuse/volt_od updates, and wrongly called the function a pure helper; the 'unknown sw_id -> clear mon mode -> return true' flow is at 2098-2100, 2113-2119. Rejections were mechanical (name) only.

name: cmd_db_ready
prose: Reports whether the Qualcomm command DB is usable; slice cut the head, real definition int cmd_db_ready(void) at cmd-db.c:133. It reads the file-static pointer cmd_db_header: if it is NULL it returns -EPROBE_DEFER (-517); else if cmd_db_magic_matches(cmd_db_header) is false it returns -EINVAL (-22); otherwise it returns 0. It takes no locks and allocates nothing. The result depends on the global cmd_db_header, which is set by the probe code.
note: Round 15 right that the old contract only bounded the result range and ignored the conditions (cmd-db.c:135-140); contract field now empty because the function reads global state (cmd_db_header) and the contract cannot express it. Return values: -EPROBE_DEFER (136), -EINVAL (138), 0 (140).

name: tegra_pmc_probe
prose: Platform probe for the Tegra PMC; slice cut the head, real definition static int tegra_pmc_probe(struct platform_device *pdev) at pmc.c:2924. It returns -ENODEV (with WARN_ON) if the global pmc->base or pmc->soc is NULL. Then each of the following returns its negative error immediately with no cleanup beyond devm: tegra_pmc_parse_dt, devm_add_action_or_reset, devm_platform_ioremap_resource (resource 0, the new base), and either for a SoC with has_single_mmio_aperture the wake/aotag/scratch pointers are all set to that base, or the 'wake' and 'aotag' resources are mapped and the optional 'scratch' resource is mapped (pmc->scratch is NULL if absent); then devm_clk_get_optional for 'pclk' (via dev_err_probe), devm_register_reboot_notifier (only when pmc->scratch is set), the restart and power-off devm_register_sys_off_handler calls, devm_clk_notifier_register and clk_get_rate (only when pmc->clk is non-NULL), and, after setting pmc->dev, tegra_pmc_init. These early failures leave already-assigned fields such as pmc->wake, pmc->aotag, pmc->scratch, pmc->clk and pmc->dev set. It then calls tegra_pmc_init_tsense_reset and tegra_pmc_reset_sysfs_init (creating the reset_reason and reset_level sysfs files), tegra_pmc_pinctrl_init and tegra_pmc_regmap_init: a failure of either goes to cleanup_sysfs, which only removes the two sysfs files and returns the error, without removing powergates. tegra_powergate_init and tegra_pmc_irq_init failures go to cleanup_powergates, which calls tegra_powergate_remove_all and then removes the two sysfs files. On success it takes powergates_lock, iounmaps the old pmc->base and stores the new base in pmc->base, registers the PMC clocks, sets drvdata, initialises suspend, applies the SoC's set_wake_filters if present, creates the 'powergate' debugfs file and returns 0. The function never returns a positive value; it frees no memory itself (devm resources are released by the driver core on probe failure).
note: Round 15 right: pinctrl and regmap init failures jump to cleanup_sysfs (pmc.c:3051-3057) which does not call tegra_powergate_remove_all (that is only at cleanup_powergates 3084-3085, reached from tegra_powergate_init and tegra_pmc_irq_init failures 3059-3065); old prose said powergates were removed on all four. pmc->base is replaced only on the success path (3067-3070). Also noted that fields assigned before a later early return stay set. Slice cut the head.

name: amd_suspend
prose: System-suspend callback for the AMD SoundWire manager (amd_manager.c:1207; slice cut the head); amd_manager = dev_get_drvdata(dev). If bus->prop.hw_disabled is set it returns 0 immediately. If power_mode_mask has AMD_SDW_CLK_STOP_MODE it calls cancel_work_sync on amd_sdw_work, disables wake signalling (amd_sdw_wake_enable(false)), when acp_rev >= ACP70_PCI_REV_ID disables host wake and returns its error if nonzero, then calls amd_sdw_clock_stop and returns its result if nonzero (amd_sdw_clock_stop logs failures but returns 0 on every path in this tree, so in practice nothing is propagated from it). Otherwise, if power_mode_mask has AMD_SDW_POWER_OFF_MODE, it does the same steps and then calls amd_deinit_sdw_manager, returning its error if nonzero. If neither mode bit is set none of that is done. In every case that gets past the hw_disabled check, if acp_rev >= ACP70_PCI_REV_ID it then sets the device state to AMD_SDW_DEVICE_STATE_D3 and returns that call's error if nonzero, even when neither mode bit was set; the function returns 0 when no step failed. It takes no locks directly.
note: Round 15 mixed: the D3 step (amd_manager.c:1249-1253) runs whenever acp_rev >= ACP70_PCI_REV_ID, independent of the mode bits, which is what the old prose said ('after the mode handling, only when acp_rev >= ACP70') but its closing clause was ambiguous; now stated explicitly. amd_sdw_clock_stop returns 0 at every return (1100, 1105, 1112, 1120). Early errors at 1225, 1229, 1236, 1244, 1247, 1252.

name: amd_suspend_runtime
prose: Runtime-suspend callback for the AMD SoundWire manager (amd_manager.c:1257; slice cut the head). If bus->prop.hw_disabled is set it returns 0 immediately. If power_mode_mask has AMD_SDW_CLK_STOP_MODE it enables wake signalling (amd_sdw_wake_enable(true)), when acp_rev >= ACP70_PCI_REV_ID enables host wake (returning its error if nonzero), then calls amd_sdw_clock_stop and returns its result if nonzero (which in this tree is always 0). Otherwise, if power_mode_mask has AMD_SDW_POWER_OFF_MODE, it does the same and then calls amd_deinit_sdw_manager, returning its error if nonzero. If neither mode bit is set none of that is done. Independent of the mode bits, when acp_rev >= ACP70_PCI_REV_ID it sets the device state to AMD_SDW_DEVICE_STATE_D3 and returns its error if nonzero, and then, if amd_manager->wake_en_mask is nonzero and ACP_PME_EN reads 0, writes 1 to ACP_PME_EN and reads it back for a debug message. It returns 0 if no step failed. It takes no locks directly.
note: Round 15 right: D3 and the PME enable (amd_manager.c:1293-1304) depend only on acp_rev >= ACP70_PCI_REV_ID, not on the mode bits; old prose said they do not happen when neither mode bit is set. Original (unconditional D3/PME) was wrong: both need acp_rev >= ACP70 (1293).

name: sdw_handle_slave_status
prose: Processes a SoundWire bus status update; slice cut the head, real definition int sdw_handle_slave_status(struct sdw_bus *bus, enum sdw_slave_status status[]) at bus.c:1910. status must have entries 0 to SDW_MAX_DEVICES. First pass over device numbers 1..SDW_MAX_DEVICES: for each slot set in bus->assigned (tested under bus->bus_lock) whose slave exists (sdw_get_slave), if status[i] is SDW_SLAVE_UNATTACHED and the slave was not already unattached it marks the slave unattached and calls sdw_update_slave_status (which notifies the driver), storing the result in ret and logging a negative value; other slots are skipped. Then, if status[0] is SDW_SLAVE_ATTACHED, it calls sdw_program_device_num and returns 0 immediately if an ID was programmed (programming errors are not checked and the first pass's ret is discarded). Second pass over the same slots: for each assigned slave found, a switch on status[i]: UNATTACHED marks the slave unattached if it was not; ALERT does nothing and continues to the next slot (skipping the update_status call below) if the slave was neither attached nor in alert, otherwise calls sdw_handle_slave_alerts; ATTACHED, when the slave was not already attached, marks it attached and, unless it was previously in alert, calls sdw_initialize_slave and notes that initialization is pending; other values only log. Except for the skipped ALERT case, it then calls sdw_update_slave_status(slave, status[i]); and, if initialization was pending, calls complete_all on initialization_complete and requests a runtime resume with pm_request_resume. Errors from alert handling, initialization and update_status are logged and do not stop the loop. The return value is the last value assigned to ret: since sdw_update_slave_status runs after the alert or initialization call in the same iteration, it is the result of the last update_status call actually made in the second pass, or, if none was made there (for example no assigned slave, or every slot skipped), the result of the last update_status call of the first pass, or 0 if none. It can therefore be 0 even after an earlier callback failure. Locks: only bus->bus_lock around the assigned-bit tests in this function; update_status callbacks run in callees.
note: Round 15 mixed: update_status is indeed not called for every assigned slave (ALERT slot in a non-attached/non-alert state is skipped by 'continue' at bus.c:1992-1994, and the first pass only handles unattached transitions), but ret from alert/initialize (1996, 2015) is always overwritten by the update_status result at 2029 in the same iteration, so the final return is never from alert/init. Round 2 right (returns the last call value, may be 0 after an earlier error, 2054). Original right (final 'return ret'). Whole function read.

name: check_frame_start
prose: Validates the header word of a BPT frame; slice cut the head, real definition static int check_frame_start(u32 header, u8 counter) at cadence_master.c:2465. It reads no memory. If bit 31 of header is clear it returns -EIO. Otherwise it calls check_counter, which returns -EIO when counter differs from the low 4 bits of the header's top byte ((header >> 24) & 0xF), and returns that error if negative. Otherwise it returns check_response(header): the 2-bit response field (header >> 3) & 3 gives -ENODATA when it is 0 (ignored), -EIO when it is not 1, and 0 when it is 1 (ACK). The result is therefore 0 exactly when bit 31 is set, the counter matches and the response field is 1; -ENODATA only when bit 31 is set, the counter matches and the response field is 0; and -EIO in all other cases. It never returns a positive value.
note: Old prose matches the code (cadence_master.c:2442-2478); the contract was dropped from the result because the earlier mechanical rejection (prose names EIO and ENODATA but the contract used bare numbers) could not be satisfied without symbolic names. Slice cut the head.

name: check_frame_end
prose: Validates the footer word of a BPT frame; slice cut the head, real definition static int check_frame_end(u32 footer) at cadence_master.c:2480. It reads no memory. If bit 30 of footer is clear it returns -EIO. Otherwise it returns check_response(footer): the 2-bit response field (footer >> 3) & 3 gives -ENODATA when it is 0 (ignored), -EIO when it is not 1, and 0 when it is 1 (ACK). The result is therefore 0 exactly when bit 30 is set and the response field is 1; -ENODATA only when bit 30 is set and the response field is 0; and -EIO in all other cases. It never returns a positive value.
note: Old prose matches the code (cadence_master.c:2452-2463, 2480-2487); contract left empty for the same mechanical reason as check_frame_start. Slice cut the head.

name: sdw_dpn_attribute_alloc(field)
prose: Generated function field##_attribute_alloc(struct device *dev, struct attribute **res, int N, int dir, const char *format_string), defined by the macro sdw_dpn_attribute_alloc(field) (sysfs_slave_dpn.c:27-49) and instantiated once per field by sdw_dpn_attr(field) and sdw_dpn_array_attr(field) (for example imp_def_interrupts_attribute_alloc). It allocates a struct dpn_attribute with devm_kzalloc(dev, ..., GFP_KERNEL); on failure it returns -ENOMEM and leaves *res untouched. On success it stores N, dir and format_string in the new object, calls sysfs_attr_init on its attribute, sets the attribute name to the stringified field name (__stringify(field)), its mode to 0444 and its show callback to field##_show, sets *res to point at the embedded struct attribute, and returns 0. The memory is device-managed (released by the driver core with the device), so the caller does not free it.
note: Macro-generated; name is the macro head per rule 5, prose describes the generated field##_attribute_alloc. The old prose omitted sysfs_attr_init (sysfs_slave_dpn.c:40); the packet prose used the imp_def_interrupts instance as if it were the only one.

name: bcm2835_spi_transfer_one_dma
prose: Runs one SPI transfer with DMA on the BCM2835 controller; slice cut the head, real definition static int bcm2835_spi_transfer_one_dma(ctlr, tfr, target, cs) at spi-bcm2835.c:770. The caller has accepted the transfer for DMA; this function itself increments count_transfer_dma and calls bcm2835_spi_transfer_prologue (which sets up the transfer state) before anything else, and undoes that prologue on its failure path. TX side: if bs->tx_buf is set it calls bcm2835_spi_prepare_sg for TX, otherwise it submits the fill_tx_desc descriptor with dmaengine_submit; a nonzero result (negative errno from prepare_sg or dma_submit_error) goes to the error label with no DMA issued. It then writes DLEN and the CS register (TA and DMAEN set), sets bs->tx_dma_active, and issues the TX DMA. RX side: if bs->rx_buf is set it prepares the RX sg list, otherwise submits target->clear_rx_desc; if that fails it calls dmaengine_terminate_sync on the TX channel, clears tx_dma_active and goes to the error label. Otherwise it issues the RX DMA and sets bs->rx_dma_active. If there is no rx_buf, TX DMA is no longer active and the cmpxchg of rx_dma_active from true to false succeeds, it terminates the RX DMA asynchronously and resets the hardware. It then returns 1 (the transfer completes asynchronously). The error label resets the hardware (bcm2835_spi_reset_hw), undoes the prologue and returns the nonzero error code. No locks are taken here.
note: Round 15 right: the prologue is called inside this function (spi-bcm2835.c:786) and tx_buf/rx_buf are tested here (789, 815), not set up by the caller; old precondition was wrong. Returns at 844 (1) and 849 (error). Slice cut the head.

name: LPSPI_BUF_RX(u8)
prose: Generated function fsl_lpspi_buf_rx_u8(struct fsl_lpspi_data *fsl_lpspi), produced by the macro LPSPI_BUF_RX(type) (spi-fsl-lpspi.c:161-170) and instantiated by LPSPI_BUF_RX(u8) at line 186. It always reads the IMX7ULP_RDR register into a local unsigned int. If fsl_lpspi->rx_buf is non-NULL it stores the low 8 bits of that value at rx_buf with a u8 store and advances rx_buf by one byte; if rx_buf is NULL it stores nothing and leaves rx_buf unchanged (the register is still read). It returns void, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Macro-generated; name is the macro invocation per rule 5. Prose matches macro body (spi-fsl-lpspi.c:164-169); the register read happens regardless of rx_buf, which the old prose already stated.

name: LPSPI_BUF_RX(u16)
prose: Generated function fsl_lpspi_buf_rx_u16(struct fsl_lpspi_data *fsl_lpspi), produced by the macro LPSPI_BUF_RX(type) (spi-fsl-lpspi.c:161-170) and instantiated by LPSPI_BUF_RX(u16) at line 188. It always reads the IMX7ULP_RDR register into a local unsigned int. If fsl_lpspi->rx_buf is non-NULL it stores the low 16 bits of that value at rx_buf with a u16 store and advances rx_buf by two bytes; if rx_buf is NULL it stores nothing and leaves rx_buf unchanged (the register is still read). It returns void, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Macro-generated; name is the macro invocation per rule 5. Prose matches macro body (spi-fsl-lpspi.c:164-169); the register read happens regardless of rx_buf, which the old prose already stated.

On normal completion it returns status, the number of bytes moved, which equals t->len whenever t->len is a multiple of the word size (two bytes when bits_per_word > 8); with an odd t->len and bits_per_word > 8, len is unsigned and the loop's 'len -= bytes' would wrap rather than end. name: stm32h7_spi_irq_thread
prose: Threaded interrupt handler for the STM32H7 SPI controller; slice cut the head, real definition static irqreturn_t stm32h7_spi_irq_thread(int irq, void *dev_id) at spi-stm32.c:1055. dev_id is the struct spi_controller pointer (not the struct stm32_spi); the stm32_spi comes from spi_controller_get_devdata(ctrl). It takes spi->lock with spin_lock_irqsave, reads SR and IER, and builds mask = IER | SUSP, adding TXP and RXP when cur_comm is SPI_FULL_DUPLEX and cur_usedma is false. If no bit of mask is set in SR it releases the lock and returns IRQ_NONE. Otherwise it handles: SUSP (when not using DMA and rx_buf and rx_len are set it reads the RX FIFO; sets end when cur_usedma); MODF (warns, sets end); OVR (logs an error, sets end); EOT (reads the RX FIFO as above when not using DMA, sets end if not using DMA, or in SPI_SIMPLEX_TX or SPI_3WIRE_TX mode, or if mdma_rx is set and the mode is SPI_SIMPLEX_RX or SPI_FULL_DUPLEX); TXP (writes the TX FIFO when not using DMA and tx_buf and tx_len are set); RXP (reads the RX FIFO when not using DMA and rx_buf and rx_len are set). It then writes (sr & mask) to IFCR to clear those events and releases the lock. If end is set: when cur_usedma and mdma_rx are both set it pauses the RX DMA channel with dmaengine_pause and returns IRQ_HANDLED without finalizing; otherwise it calls stm32h7_spi_disable and spi_finalize_current_transfer(ctrl) (both after the lock was released). It returns IRQ_HANDLED on every path other than the IRQ_NONE case.

If any mapping call returns nonzero it calls __spi_unmap_msg, which unmaps every mapped tx and rx table of the message and clears all tx_sg_mapped and rx_sg_mapped flags, and returns that call's error. On success it returns 0; transfers skipped by can_dma or with a NULL buffer keep their sg_mapped flag false (the function does not clear flags on the success path). It takes no locks.

name: fmh_gpib_dma_read
prose: Receives up to length bytes from the FMH GPIB board using DMA; slice cut the head, real definition static int fmh_gpib_dma_read(board, buffer, length, end, bytes_read) at fmh_gpib.c:711. It sets *bytes_read and *end to 0 and returns 0 if length is 0. It maps e_priv->dma_buffer with dma_map_single (a mapping error is only logged and execution continues), calls fmh_gpib_config_dma(board, 0) and, if that returns nonzero, unmaps the buffer and returns that value; then prepares the slave DMA descriptor, and if that returns NULL it unmaps the buffer and returns -EIO. Otherwise it sets the descriptor callback to fmh_gpib_dma_callback, takes board->spinlock to program the FIFO counter and DMA enables, submits and issues the DMA and sets DMA_READ_IN_PROGRESS_BN, releases the spinlock and waits with wait_event_interruptible for DMA completion, RECEIVED_END, DEV_CLEAR or timeout. A nonzero wait result sets retval to -ERESTARTSYS, a timeout then overrides it with -ETIMEDOUT, and DEV_CLEAR then overrides that with -EINTR. It stops the DMA enables, sleeps 10 to 15 microseconds, and reads the DMA residue; if the residue is above length or negative it returns -EFAULT at once (WARN_ON_ONCE), before *bytes_read is updated, and without terminating the DMA or unmapping the buffer. Otherwise it adds length - residue to *bytes_read, calls dmaengine_terminate_all, calls fmh_gpib_dma_callback(board) if DMA_READ_IN_PROGRESS_BN is still set, and only then unmaps the buffer and copies *bytes_read bytes from the DMA buffer to buffer. It then drains any remaining bytes from the RX FIFO into buffer while *bytes_read stays below length. Under board->spinlock it sets *end to 1 only if *bytes_read > 0, READ_READY_BN is clear and RECEIVED_END_BN was set (clearing it). It returns retval: 0, or -ERESTARTSYS, -ETIMEDOUT or -EINTR from the wait handling (with -EINTR over -ETIMEDOUT over -ERESTARTSYS). The spinlock is released on every path where it was taken. The caller keeps ownership of buffer.

Round 2 right: on the config and descriptor error returns *bytes_read stays 0 (735-747, bytes_read updated only at 790). name: hp82335_attach

It sets board->status to 0 and allocates the private data with hp82335_allocate_private (failure returns -ENOMEM), sets up the TMS9914 register accessors and offset, and then validates config->ibbase against the 15 supported addresses 0xc4000 to 0xfc000 in steps of 0x4000; any other value logs an error and returns -EINVAL (the private data allocated before this check is not freed here). It returns 0 on success. This function does not release anything it acquired on any failure path (private data, memory region, ioremap mapping); resources are left for the detach path.
